audience.text: Python developers who need to generate, modify, or process PowerPoint presentations programmatically without relying on Microsoft Office or external rendering engines.

capabilities.text: Create new presentations from scratch and open existing .pptx files for reading or modification.
capabilities.title: Presentation I/O

capabilities.text: Add, remove, clone, hide, and reorder slides; add AutoShapes, PictureFrames, Tables, Connectors, and GroupShapes.
capabilities.title: Slide and shape management

capabilities.text: Format text at portion, paragraph, and text frame levels including font properties, bullets, alignment, and hyperlinks.
capabilities.title: Text formatting

capabilities.text: Insert 73 chart types backed by embedded XLSX workbooks, configure series, categories, axes, trendlines, and data labels.
capabilities.title: Charts and data

capabilities.text: Set slide transition types, timing, and advance settings; support for shape and text animations with sequences and effects.
capabilities.title: Slide transitions and animations

capabilities.text: Add speaker notes per slide and manage comment authors, comments, and replies with timestamps and positions.
capabilities.title: Comments and notes

capabilities.text: Set built-in and custom document properties such as title, author, keywords, and custom metadata.
capabilities.title: Document properties

capabilities.text: Embed images from bytes or file-like objects using Presentation.images.add_image and add_picture_frame.
capabilities.title: Image embedding

limitations.text: Only seven SaveFormat values produce valid output files; fourteen raise ValueError for unsupported formats including PDF, HTML, XPS, TIFF, GIF, ODP, OTP, FODP, XML, and legacy binary PowerPoint formats.
Rendering and conversion to PDF, HTML, XPS, or image formats is not implemented; the library writes OOXML, not rendered output.
Presentation sections are not supported; Presentation.sections does not exist.
Slide size cannot be read or changed via public API; new presentations use the bundled template default (16:9).
SmartArt, OLE objects, mathematical text, VBA macros, digital signatures, and encryption are not implemented.
add_image requires image bytes or a file-like object; it does not accept a file path directly.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic creation and modification of PowerPoint presentations using pure Python code without requiring Microsoft Office or external dependencies.
Supports embedding and managing charts with embedded XLSX workbooks, allowing dynamic data-driven presentations.
Provides support for slide transitions, animations, comments, notes, and document properties to produce feature-complete presentations.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Slides FOSS for Python is an open-source Python library for creating, reading, and editing PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations.

uncertainties: The exact set of supported chart types beyond the 73 named in the public symbol list is not specified.
Whether Markdown export supports all 24 flavors mentioned in the README is not confirmed by public symbols.
The behavior of comment thread preservation when comment authors are modified is described in the README but not directly verified by public symbols.

workflows.name: Create new presentation
workflows.text: Instantiate a Presentation object, add shapes, text, tables, or charts, and save as .pptx using SaveFormat.PPTX.

workflows.name: Edit existing presentation
workflows.text: Load a .pptx file using Presentation('file.pptx'), modify slides, shapes, text, or formatting, and re-save.

workflows.name: Add charts with data
workflows.text: Create a chart with add_chart, access its embedded workbook via chart_data_workbook, populate cells, and bind series/categories to cell references.

workflows.name: Export to Markdown
workflows.text: Save presentation text content as Markdown using SaveFormat.MD with configurable flavor options.
